body: Ind AS 116/IFRS 16 (from 1-Apr-2019) put nearly every lease on balance sheet; P&L shows depreciation + interest (rent leaves opex, EBITDA rises) and cash principal/interest sits in financing (CFO rises). US ASC 842 operating leases are also on balance sheet but the P&L shows one straight-line lease cost in opex and cash stays in CFO. Worked example INDIGO adoption (Screener): FY19 -> FY20 borrowings incl. leases 2,429 -> 22,719; depreciation 760 -> 3,974; interest 563 -> 1,902; EBITDA -149 -> 4,090; CFO 3,176 -> 6,972. Restating FY20 pre-116 (subtract incremental D&A + interest 4,553) gives EBITDA ~ -463, i.e. the business worsened while reported EBITDA swung +4,239. FY26: borrowings 77,749, depreciation 10,808, interest 5,944, PAT -2,394. Rule: for Indian airlines, retailers, hospitals, QSRs subtract total lease payments from EBITDA and CFO before comparing with US peers or pre-FY20 history; use lease-adjusted net debt / EBITDAR.
title: Lease accounting break: Ind AS 116 inflates EBITDA and CFO vs US ASC 842 (IndiGo worked)
